clue.text: After complicated ascent, line makes descent

indicators.note: complicated tells us the letters of ascent are tangled into a new order

parts.note: RY, short for railway, is a standard crossword line

explanation.surface: A climber, having made a tricky ascent, finds a rope line for the way down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' only orders the pieces; 'complicated' scrambles the ascent. 'descent' at the end looks like the opposite of ascent but means ancestry, and RY (railway) is the usual crossword line.
explanation.definitionFit: Descent in the sense of lineage or family origins is a synonym.

clue.text: A secondary route out of the country

parts.note: Britain grades minor routes as B-class, one level below the main A routes, hence B plus the word for a way

explanation.surface: A minor road leads overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, B-class roads are secondary routes below A roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas, in a foreign land.

clue.text: Qualified to pound out whole books

indicators.note: out says the symbol for a pound comes away from the word for whole

parts.note: complete means whole
L is the symbol for a pound sterling
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone is qualified to bash through entire books.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop L (pound) from COMPLETE to get COMPETE, then add NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable, having the needed skill or certificates.

clue.text: One animal from a pair that's left

parts.note: a span is a pair of horses or oxen yoked together
IE, from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: One beast is taken from a pair, the one that remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is read as 'that is', abbreviated IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog breed, so one particular creature.

clue.text: Funny kind of game…

definitions.meaning: odd or peculiar, old-fashioned British slang
a card game of collecting sets and runs

explanation.definitionFit: Odd in British slang, and a card game based on melding sets.

clue.text: Record curves round in grate

indicators.note: round signals turning the whole run of record plus curves backwards

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
arcs are curves

explanation.surface: Someone sets a record, curving it round inside a fireplace grate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns the record and the curves together as one run, not each in place; 'grate' is a verb here, not the fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: To grate on a surface is to rub it harshly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: …one in which strikers go through the hoop

definitions.text: one in which strikers go through the hoop

parts.words: one in which strikers go through the hoop
parts.note: continuing the game of 4 down: a lawn game where mallet-hit balls must pass through wire arches

explanation.surface: Footballers having a terrible time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go through the hoop' is a British idiom for suffering an ordeal; here it is literal, balls hit through hoops on a lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn sport played with mallets driving balls through metal arches.

clue.text: The prize is a watch

parts.note: ward means guard or watch, as in 'watch and ward'

explanation.surface: The winner's reward turns out to be a wristwatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize given to a winner.

clue.text: Characters of old used in Time to see the sights of fabulous city

indicators.note: used in puts the shuffled letters inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: Characters of means the letters of old, taken in a new order

parts.note: to do a city is to see its sights

explanation.surface: Ancient writing is consulted to visit a legendary city's attractions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters of' rearranges the three letters of old, and 'used in' sets them inside the period of time. To 'do' a city is to tour its sights; El Dorado is the mythical city of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary South American city of gold, fabled rather than real.

clue.text: Sword, that's one to damage it internally

parts.note: sc., from Latin scilicet, means namely or that is
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: internally places the word it inside the word for damage

parts.note: to mar is to damage

explanation.surface: A blade, which is one tool for wrecking something from within.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is read as the Latin scilicet, namely, abbreviated SC; 'internally' sets the word it inside the verb for spoiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved Oriental sabre, a kind of blade.

clue.text: Labour leader took sheep, for instance, to old farmer

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
say means for instance, as in 'take, say, ten'
Old MacDonald had a farm in the nursery song

explanation.surface: A Labour politician has taken sheep, for example, to an elderly farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took' and 'to' simply join the pieces. Ramsay MacDonald was Britain's first Labour Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the first Labour Party prime minister of Britain, leading it in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Something pleasant can be changed any time

indicators.note: can be changed tells us the letters of any time may be reordered

explanation.surface: A nice thing about a plan is that you can alter it whenever you like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be changed' rearranges the seven letters of ANY TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant feature or facility of a place, such as a park, is a synonym.

clue.text: One giving shape to crumble

definitions.meaning: a person who forms material in a mould

explanation.definitionFit: One who forms things in a cast; also a verb for rotting away to powder.

clue.text: Compact expression of intent from Madame Defarge & Co.

definitions.text: expression of intent from Madame Defarge & Co.
definitions.meaning: Madame Defarge and her fellow women in Dickens's A Tale of Two Cities knit beside the guillotine, so they announce they will do so

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense hears the hyphenated word as a contraction of 'we will' plus the verb for working wool.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturdy, solid build is described this way; read as a phrase it is the knitters' declaration of what they will do.

clue.text: Young bird settling comfortably

definitions.meaning: a chick too young to leave its nest

explanation.definitionFit: A chick still in the nest; also snuggling down cosily.

clue.text: Stamp trade out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of trade are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: Commerce in postage stamps has come to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles TRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp is to put a foot down heavily, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Soldiers get up before general, with church coming out

indicators.note: get up, in a down clue, sends the soldiers upwards, reversing them

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Troops rise ahead of their general, as the church service ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up' reverses the corps (Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers) as a down clue reads upward; 'before' and 'with' only join the pieces. 'coming out' at the end looks like part of the story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of emerging or appearing, a noun synonym.

clue.text: It's cheap, making an imitation work

indicators.note: making suggests the letters of it's cheap are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something copied from another artist is cheaply done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges ITSCHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A work deliberately copying the style of another artist or period.

clue.text: Flower Diana's plucked from catastrophe

indicators.note: plucked from says one word is pulled out of another

parts.note: a disaster is a catastrophe
Di is short for Diana; with the possessive it becomes DI'S

explanation.surface: Princess Diana's flower is snatched out of a calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap catastrophe for its synonym DISASTER, then pluck out DIS (Di's) from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a daisy-like garden bloom, often purple, one kind of plant in bloom.

clue.text: Score in game put up or down

definitions.meaning: a run scored in the bat-and-ball game ...
one who rounds a number up or down

explanation.walkthrough: Rounders is a British schoolyard game rather like baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: A run in the British bat-and-ball game rounders; also someone approximating figures to the nearest whole.

clue.text: A second output device for computer, one going fast

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a printer turns computer files into paper copies

explanation.surface: A computer user buys a second printing machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who races at top speed over short distances.

clue.text: Spotted, like a plain cake

definitions.meaning: a plain cake has no frosting on top

explanation.definitionFit: Seen or observed; split in two, it describes a bun without frosting.

clue.text: Fair ladies, one of them titled, in New York

definitions.text: one of them titled, in New York
definitions.meaning: an 1897 Broadway musical comedy takes its title from one such beauty of New York

explanation.definitionFit: Pretty women; and one of them gives the title of the musical about a New York beauty.

clue.text: What finishes out (true!) of touch

indicators.note: What finishes points to the closing letter of the word out

parts.note: actual means real or true

explanation.surface: Someone protests that being out of touch is the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What finishes out' is the T at the end of OUT; the brackets and exclamation are decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the sense of feel, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Ruler of half a state

indicators.note: half takes the opening five of the ten letters of the state

parts.note: California is a US state

explanation.surface: A governor controls half of a country's territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first half of CALIFORNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of caliph, a Muslim sovereign.

clue.text: Weariness of posh soldier retreating in downfall

indicators.note: in says the reversed pair sits inside the word for downfall

parts.note: fate can mean doom or ruin, a downfall

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the posh-soldier pair is reversed

parts.note: U means upper-class or posh
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An upper-class soldier, withdrawing during a collapse, is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns the posh-soldier pair round to IGU, which 'in' places inside the downfall; 'downfall' is fate in the sense of ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme tiredness is a synonym.

clue.text: A little bit of adverse criticism has point

parts.note: flak is hostile criticism
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Even a small amount of hostile feedback has a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thin fragment, such as of snow or paint.

clue.text: Shuffle & Co. an alliance producing liquid asset in Scotland

indicators.note: Shuffle is an order to mix up the letters that follow

parts.note: the ampersand stands for and
Co. is short for company, written CO

explanation.surface: Some business partnership shuffles its company into an alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffle' mixes AND (from &), CO, AN and ALLIANCE. The liquid asset is a waterway across the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a canal of fresh water running across the Highlands, cheekily called an asset that is liquid.

clue.text: Try putting a little iron round stronghold

indicators.note: round turns the symbol for a small bit of iron backwards

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, a short form of it
a fort is a stronghold

explanation.surface: A smith tries putting some iron around a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a container signal, but it reverses the iron symbol, which then sits before the stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt, a noun synonym.

clue.text: 18 is such a master

parts.note: the solution to 18 across is the word master with its first letter removed, so the master has lost its top

explanation.surface: A flower is a kind of expert, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 across is ASTER: knock the M off MASTER and that is what remains, a master without its top.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a top part, as a word missing its first letter is described.
